To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in 2-kidney, one clip hypertension (2K1CH), the expression of cyclooxygenase (COX)-1, COX-2, and prostaglandin (PG)E synthase (PGS) is differentially affected by the action of ANG II and bradykinin (BK) on the clipped and the nonclipped kidneys and that COX-1 expression may be a target of the ANG II system.
in renovascular hypertensive rats, renal COX-1 expression was decreased in both kidneys and COX-1 was not regulated by ANG II or B(2) receptors.

in early renal hypertensive rats the expression of the COX isoforms and prostaglandin synthase is not uniform, and is modulated by ANG II and bradykinin, and the resulting renal prostaglandins have an important role in the pathogenesis of renovascular hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of renal COX-1 in the regulation of renal volume in early renovascular hypertensive disease.
the role of the renal COX isoforms and related components in early renovascular hypertensive rats.
the regulation of renal COX-1, COX-2, and related products in early 2K1c renovascular hypertension, and the impact of ANG II receptor and B(2) bradykinin receptor blockade on this regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regulation of COX isoform expression in the kidney is complex and involves several mechanisms.
the regulation of the COX isoform expression and function is complex, and the regulation of the expression and function of the downstream enzyme PGES is not well understood.
in renovascular hypertension COX-1, PGES, and COX2 are regulated by ANG II and bradykinin in a kidney-specific fashion, and that this may contribute to the pathophysiology of hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
COX-1, but not COX-2, is downregulated by renovascular hypertension and that this downregulation is independent of NO.
the renal cortical expression of COX-isoforms and related enzymes is regulated by ANG II and B(2) receptors, and that the expression of COX and PGES is not necessarily coordinated.
the COX-1/PGES system is a key regulator of renal volume and function, and its expression is regulated by ANG II, B(2) receptors, and NOS1 in a kidney-specific manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
COX-1 is regulated differently than COX-2 in 2K-1C hypertension.
COX isoforms may be differentially regulated in the kidney in renovascular hypertension, and that this may be a mechanism to modulate the renal response to hypertension.

COX-1 expression is not uniformly reduced in the cortex in 2KIC, but rather, the downregulation of COX- 1 and PGES selectively in the nonclipping kidney may be a compensatory mechanism in response to the increased activity in the clipping kidney.
